dossier.architecture: Turret shooter with finger-fed cargo and a rotating windmill climber.

subsystems.drivetrain: Exact drive hardware remains unresolved in this review.
subsystems.intake: Compliant four-bar rebuilt after Orange County because earlier rollers kicked cargo away.
subsystems.transfer: Sensors count cargo; three-finger popper presents it to the launcher, drawing on the team's 2012 solution.
subsystems.scoring: Full-turn turret; Orange County two-position pneumatic hood replaced by adjustable rack. Main treaded wheel and smaller top wheels maintain compression.
subsystems.endgame: Complex pneumatic Orange County sequence replaced by gas-shock rotating windmill; deployment actuator also changed.
subsystems.controls: Limelight lookup tables set range parameters; LEDs communicate inventory, tracking and shot readiness.

versions: Post-Orange-County collector, hood and climber revisions are established.
Color rejection was a future Champs goal at filming, not an observed capability.
dossier.analysis: A finger feeder is an architectural alternative to continuously squeezing cargo through rollers. Its value depends on controlled release timing, while collector and hood revisions show why a reveal cannot stand for an entire season.
limits: Only the reviewed published configurations are established; intermediate changes may be undocumented.

context_documents.title: 2022-987 · An intake rebuild and hood change solve different range/flow limits
context_documents.body:
# 2022-987: An intake rebuild and hood change solve different range/flow limits

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

After Orange County, a compliant four-bar replaces collector behavior that kicked cargo away. A three-finger popper presents cargo; the retained record distinguishes an early two-position hood from a later adjustable rack.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly reports the initial pickup failure and credits a historical in-team popper concept.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A mechanism lineage is useful because it carries operating experience, not because old geometry is automatically optimal. Keep the collector and hood revisions separate; improved range cannot be assigned to the collector alone.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test moving cargo acquisition and popper timing, then compare hood-range performance at controlled incoming velocity.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://youtu.be/0ERsLAOju40](https://youtu.be/0ERsLAOju40)

source_reviews.title: Behind the Bumpers with the High Rollers at Las Vegas
source_reviews.locator: 1:35–3:17 collector and popper; 3:30–4:55 hood and turret; 5:05–6:27 climber; 6:35–8:25 status and targeting
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the full available English automatic caption track, including the start and end. Technical details are attributed to team speakers. No visual inspection claimed.
facts: The compliant-wheel collector followed an Orange County version that kicked cargo away.
A three-finger popper presented cargo to the shooter. The team drew on its 2012 design.
A rack-and-pinion adjustment replaced the two-position pneumatic hood. The team also changed the climb sequence.
source_reviews.limitations: The interview describes Las Vegas and retrospects Orange County. Some transmission wording is ambiguous. Color sorting was a planned Champs addition.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: The Las Vegas High Rollers robot used a four-bar pickup, a two-position inventory in its transport, and a deliberate final upward presentation into a separately aimed launcher. That final presentation is the unusual choice. A staged cargo waits for an actuator to put it into the shooting contacts. The pickup and hood revisions address different failures: bouncing off the robot before possession and limited control of release after possession.
piece_flow: The four-bar places compliant wheels in contact with floor cargo and passes it into the indexer.
Inventory sensing distinguishes one and two cargo. The second waits for the first to clear.
The three fingers lift the staged ball into the treaded main and smaller upper wheels. The turret and adjustable hood establish the shot.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The popper needs a clear approach below the shooting contacts while the turret yaws through its reported full-turn sweep from one limit to the other. The interviews describe a fixed sensor used to signal cargo at the popper and a camera mounted to the turret. Check the overlap between the moving shooter and fixed presentation throughout yaw, along with the cable sweep and climber travel.

subsystems.name: Compliant four-bar
subsystems.construction: Four-bar deployment with compliant pickup wheels.
subsystems.operation: Capture the ball with compression and pass it into the indexer.
subsystems.team_rationale: Earlier contacts could send cargo across the field instead of collecting it.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Wheel compliance can absorb a poor approach, but a soft wheel may still kick a fast ball if the entry path lacks a closing contact.
subsystems.interfaces: The last pickup contact must keep custody until the indexer accepts the ball.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test centered and glancing approaches with stationary and rolling cargo. Inspect wheel wear and asymmetric deployment.
subsystems.unknowns: Wheel material, preload and changes to links are unverified.

subsystems.name: Indexer and three-finger popper
subsystems.construction: Sensors distinguish inventory and an ultrasonic sensor reports cargo at the popper. Three fingers support the staged ball.
subsystems.operation: Raise the ball into the launcher after the first piece clears.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team recalled jams with its 2020 uptake and cited consistent presentation on its 2012 popper.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A fixed launch entry can improve repeatability, but the popper return adds a time and clearance constraint.
subsystems.interfaces: A second cargo must remain out of the fingers’ return path. Presence and shooter-ready states are distinct.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Observe short lifts and check whether the next piece can be staged after a weak or interrupted shot.
subsystems.unknowns: Actuator geometry and fault recovery are unknown.

subsystems.name: Launcher and vision
subsystems.construction: Treaded six-inch main wheels, smaller upper wheels and rack-and-pinion adjustment in the interview configuration.
subsystems.operation: Use camera-derived range and tuned speed and hood settings, with separate moving and stationary indications.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team found treaded contacts consistent and wanted more range control than the earlier hood gave.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A range table is sensitive to consistent entry and contact compression. Dynamic shots add sensitivity to velocity estimates and latency.
subsystems.interfaces: The popper, wheel recovery, turret position and vision validity must agree before release.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test loss of target just after a feed command and inspect binding near the yaw limits.
subsystems.unknowns: No verified speed maps, wire routing or shot dispersion.

subsystems.name: Windmill climb
subsystems.construction: Rotating traversal geometry with gas-shock assistance and a piston reported for deployment.
subsystems.operation: Deploy and transfer between bars by rotating through the climb.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team replaced much of the earlier complex pneumatic sequence and reported a faster deployment.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Fewer sequential actions help only if hook engagement remains tolerant of bar approach and chassis swing.
subsystems.interfaces: Plot climb sweep against the shooter and neighboring hang positions.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check incomplete deployment and a single-side catch on a fixture.
subsystems.unknowns: Load paths and capture tolerances are unverified.

revisions: Orange County pickup, hood and climb preceded the Las Vegas versions.
transferable_principles: Use positive presentation where a repeatable launch entry is worth an extra indexing motion.
Display possession and shot readiness independently.
disconfirming_conditions: A continuously supported roller path may cycle faster if it matches popper presentation repeatability.
A fixed shooter changes the approach and readiness timing, so remeasure the entire cycle.
remaining_gaps: Worlds sorting installation, climb geometry and as-built yaw limits.
recommended_images: Request a side view with popper down and fully raised, plus the turret at both yaw limits.
